newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's debt to gain most from lira's ERM re-entry.
newsitem.headline: Spain's debt to gain most from lira's ERM re-entry.

text.p: Spanish bonds are likely to outperform Italian BTPs in coming weeks though both markets could first experience a profit-taking wave as initial euphoria on the lira's ERM re-entry wanes, analysts said on Monday.
Analysts said Italy's step toward European Monetary Union (EMU) would benefit all peripheral countries over the long term.
"The fact that Italy has increased its possibilities of entering EMU could be positive for all peripheral markets," said Carmen Hernansanz, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Spanish bonos held gains made after the long-anticipated return of Italy's lira to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

But near- to medium-term, dealers said the lengthy meeting in Brussels to hash out the 990 lira-mark parity was a bad sign, suggesting political difficulties lay ahead among members of the forthcoming union.
"The market is taking the news as good, but the fact they needed two days to get an agreement was bad," said Tierry Loiseau, dealer at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
At 1200 GMT, the long-term Bonos future contract was down 3 basis points (bps) at 111.17, not far from its all-time high of 111.45 made on Thursday.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was at 129 bps, after hitting a new record low of 128 bps.

The differential between Spain's debt and BTPs was around 45 basis points after news Italian prosecutor was seeking trial for Prime Minister Prodi over "abuse of office" when he was head of State holding IRI.
"We could see the spread under BTPs decline, maybe to 35 bps for the initial euphoria. But I expect it to widen then above 50 bps," said Loiseau.
Loiseau forecast a possible correction lower in the Spanish future to 110.50.
"They needed two days to get an agreement...a correction could take place at this point, and bonos are set to outperform Italians," said Robert Huw, strategist at Natwest in London.
He said he expected the differential between Spanish and Italian 10-year bonds to widen to around 60 and 70 basis points before the end of the year.
"No major movements are likely this week, with Thanksgiving (holiday) in the States. But I'd expect the correction sometime before the end of the year," Huw said.

The only respite for Italy's bonds is an expected sharp reduction in Italian November inflation to 2.6 percent year-on-year from 3.0 pct in October that would leave Spain lagging behind. October Spanish CPI was 3.5 percent, and official November data are scheduled for December 13.
But analysts said that was little comfort for Italian bonds. Apart from the inflation trend, Italy's fundamentals are still worse than Spain's, they said.
"The inflation trend is better in Italy, but deficit and debt are worse. We think that the Spanish market will decline less than Italian," said Loiseau.
In other markets, the lira's re-entry into the ERM had very little effect on the peseta, given market conviction the Bank of Spain is preventing the peseta from further appreciation.

It was at 84.10/4.12 versus the mark after opening at 84.08/11, and dealers said they feared the Bank of Spain could intervene to brake any sharp rise. The peseta was also trading little changed versus the lira at 11.78.
Spanish shares were also little moved by Italy's news but moved higher in line with other European markets.
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
